title: Нагиев замечает поваров в зале  (Nagiyev Spots the Cooks on the Floor)

segments.t: Spotting Senya, Fedya, and Lyova carrying plates across the dining room floor right in front of the visiting film director, a horrified Nagiyev excuses himself from the table. He pulls Vika and Chef Barinov aside and is outraged to learn that the waitresses never showed up for their shift.
Вы не знаете, где ваши подчиненные?
Знаете, о чем это говорит, а?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.

'What on earth are the cooks doing in the dining room?' Questioning whether what on earth are the cooks doing in the dining room is how Barinov tests Lyova's story. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.

'What is the meaning of this?' By wondering what the meaning of this is, Lyova presses Barinov for a straight answer. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
'The cooks are personally bringing out what they prepared.' Claiming that the cooks are personally bringing out what they prepared sounds confident, even if Lyova has doubts.

'What the hell are you people doing, huh?' When Lyova asks if what the hell are Barinov people doing huh, Barinov has to answer fast. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
'We will fix everything right now.' Barinov explains that they will fix everything right now, keeping his voice calm and direct.
'So to speak.' With the plan and table in play, Lyova keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
'Follow me, right now.' Barinov explains that Lyova should follow him right now, keeping his voice calm and direct.

'What is going on in our restaurant?' Asking what going on in their restaurant is is how Lyova puts Barinov on the spot. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
'They did not show up for work today.' Admitting that they did not show up for work today shows Barinov being honest for a change.

'What do you mean, they did not show up?' By wondering what Barinov means they did not show up, Lyova presses Barinov for a straight answer. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
Вы не знаете, где ваши подчиненные?

'You do not even know where your own subordinates are?' Asking whether Lyova does not even know where Lyova's own subordinates are puts Lyova right on the defensive. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Знаете, о чем это говорит, а?
'Do you know what that says about you, huh?' Checking whether Barinov knows what that says about Barinov huh is how Lyova puts Barinov on the spot.
'And you know, the old man is right.' Barinov tells Lyova that the old man is right without dressing it up. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Вы не знаете, где ваши подчиненные?
Знаете, о чем это говорит, а?

That wraps up this scene as stunned to see line cooks serving tables in front of the film director, Nagiyev drags Chef Barinov and Vika aside and learns that none of the waitresses came to work. See you next time!
